free_tier.stated: 5 TB of shared space on the free tier, 20 GB per file, and no upload speed cap
free_tier.notes: the landing page and the register page agree on 5 TB and 20 GB; the help centre adds 20 GB free and 30 GB for Standard members

per_object_cap.stated: 20 GB per file on the free tier; 30 GB on Standard
per_object_cap.notes: terms section 3.2.8 states the same two numbers as a default

retention.stated: files are deleted after 30 consecutive days without a sign-in on a free account, or 365 days on a paid account
retention.notes: terms section 3.2.5, quoted; the landing page states it as 'log in once a month to renew'

egress.terms: downloads are metered by tier rather than by byte: free accounts have no published volume cap but a slow channel, Standard is stated at 'up to 5MB/sec', and Super removes the limit; no per-GB egress price is published

tooling: first-party desktop client and a WebDAV endpoint; the free tier advertises WebDAV and the Super tier advertises 'WebDAV batch download'; the nfd-parser project ships a ct driver
chaining: the only Chinese pan in this survey that a foreigner can self-register for with an email address alone, so it is the one that can sit under a self-hosted bridge without a +86 number

limits.value: 30 consecutive days without a sign-in deletes files on a free account
20 GB per file on the free tier
200,000 files and 10,000 folders per account; 10,000 file uploads per day; 5 concurrent download and 5 concurrent upload threads

identity_cost.detail: the register page offers email and password as the primary path with 'Sign up with phone instead' as the alternative; no card, no ID, no +86 requirement stated

reliability_note: Over-quota triggers deletion of the excess without prior notice, and the inactivity clock deletes a free account's files at 30 days; a monthly sign-in cron keeps it alive and nothing else does.

evidence.proved: the signup form offers Email and Password with a human-verification step, and states 'Sign up with phone instead'; the page advertises 5TB free, 20GB per file, and 'Direct link sharing, WebDAV and online media playback'
'Free users: Max 20GB per file / Standard members: Max 30GB per file', and the registration steps are email, password, email verification with no identity document

section 3.2.5 deletes stored files after 30 consecutive days without sign-in on a free account; 3.2.7 caps an account at 200,000 files and 10,000 uploads per day; 3.2.8 caps a file at 20GB; 3.2.9 caps 5 concurrent download and 5 concurrent upload threads
'Free users enjoy 5TB shared space, upgrade to membership for up to 70TB'; Standard CNY 28/month or CNY 98/year; Super CNY 38/month or CNY 258/year with 10TB shared and 2TB private
free users get 5 TB of shared space
evidence.quote: Free users enjoy 5TB shared space, upgrade to membership for up to 70TB storage

evidence.proved: the per-file cap on a free account is 20 GB
long-term inactivity of about 30 days on a free account clears its files
evidence.quote: (~30 days for free users; ~365 days for paid members)

evidence.proved: the registration form takes an email and password with a phone alternative

notes: 5 TB free, 20 GB per file, email-only registration, WebDAV advertised. The 30-day inactivity deletion is the number that decides how it can be used: a monthly cron job keeps it, and nothing else does. Terms section 3.2.7 also caps the account at 200,000 files, which at 20 GB per file is a 4 PB nominal ceiling and therefore not the constraint.

extras.webdav_tier: advertised on the free tier and on Super as batch download

binding_note: The identity gate is the one that usually closes a Chinese pan, and this one is open; what binds is the 30-day inactivity clock, which makes it a working set and not an archive.
